<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "problem_statement": "One more thing — we had a login issue last week. It turned out to be our VPN, not Keelwater. Just wanted to clarify that. Last week’s ‘Keelwater is down’ report was actually caused by our own VPN — not",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "date": "2026-09-19T09:57:00+00:00",
   "quote": "One more thing — we had a login issue last week. It turned out to be our VPN, not Keelwater. Just wanted to clarify that. Last week’s ‘Keelwater is down’ report was actually caused by our own VPN — not a product issue, just a customer login outage we need to track better.",
   "route": "onboarding"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-09-14T10:19:00+00:00",
   "quote": "We’ve had a few false alarms lately where Keelwater appears down, but it’s actually our own customer network failure — maybe the sign-on provider or our VPN acting up again.",
   "route": "support"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-10-24T14:35:00+00:00",
   "quote": "We’ve had three people report the same customer login outage today, and it’s holding up claims processing — I’d appreciate any insight from your end.",
   "route": "support"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-10-27T11:53:00+00:00",
   "quote": "I’ve ruled out our own systems — it’s definitely a customer network failure, not Keelwater being down, though the error message makes it sound like a bug.",
   "route": "support"
  },
  {
   "date": "2026-09-17T13:03:00+00:00",
   "quote": "Hi Deryn, we’re having trouble getting into Keelwater this morning — our team says it’s down again. Our team keeps saying Keelwater is down, but it turns out it’s our own sign-on service failing — customer network failure is the real issue. We thought the platform was offline, but it’s actually our VPN or email system causing the login issue",
   "route": "account_management"
  }
 ],
 "title": "One more thing — we had a login issue last week. It"
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "The customer explicitly clarifies that the 'Keelwater is down' reports were caused by their own VPN/sign-on service, not the product. All quotes consistently attribute the login failures to the customer's own network, VPN, or sign-on provider. One quote mentions the error message 'makes it sound like a bug,' which could hint at a confusing error message, but the customer's own framing and the problem statement confirm the cause is outside Keelwater's product.", "verdict": "fail"}
